Speculative Decoding Methods.
We consider the loss-
less method and six lossy speculative decoding methods:

Baselines.
We use target model autoregressive decoding as the primary reference for generation
quality and latency. We compare Nucleus Sampling (NS), which modifies the sampling distribution
through temperature and nucleus truncation. Standard speculative decoding (SD) [4, 17] serves
as the exact distribution-preserving acceleration baseline. We further compare with relaxed
speculative verification methods, including ASD [10], Cactus [13], and MARS [23], which trade
exact verification guarantees for improved acceptance or efficiency. As for decoding parameters,
all methods use temperature T = 1.0. For Nucleus Sampling, we use top −p = 0.95 following the
common decoding configuration. For NSD, we set the nucleus threshold θ = 0.95 in the main
experiments.
